back_blurb: Boxes everywhere, and a goodbye to every room. [Name] packs the first-night box, holds the key to a new front door, and finds that the best bits of bedtime come too.
honesty_line: Illustrated from [Name]'s photo and checked by a person before print.
cover_art: [Name] in the story's key scene from spread 1 — face large and front-on; upper third calm for the title. Old home hall full of boxes, drawn from the inside only. [Name] holds [Object] tight; [Carer] crouches beside

title_page.spot: Small spot of the first-night box. No child on this page.

must_not_show: crying alone, no lost pet, no arguments, no "you'll forget your old friends"
child holding a box in the car
bed under a window or near blind cords

spreads.text: Boxes in the hall. Boxes in the kitchen. Boxes on [Name]'s bed. Home sounds different, all echoey. "We're moving to a new home," says [Carer]. [Name] holds [Object] tight.
spreads.setting: Old home hall full of boxes, drawn from the inside only. [Name] holds [Object] tight
spreads.art: Old home hall full of boxes, drawn from the inside only. [Name] holds [Object] tight; [Carer] crouches beside
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: "Let's say goodbye properly," says [Carer]. So they do. "Goodbye, kitchen." "Goodbye, bath." "Goodbye, the step where I put my wellies on."
spreads.setting: Old kitchen, half packed. [Name] waves goodbye
spreads.art: Old kitchen, half packed. [Name] waves goodbye; [Carer] beside
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Name]'s bedroom is last. "Goodbye, window. Goodbye, wall where my drawings were." Then [Carer] takes a photo of [Name] by the old front door.
spreads.setting: Old front door, seen close from the hall or doorstep (works for a house or a flat). [Name] on the step
spreads.art: Old front door, seen close from the hall or doorstep (works for a house or a flat). [Name] on the step; [Carer] takes a photo with a phone (blank screen)
spreads.calm_zone_note: Above the door — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Next, [Name] packs a very important box: the first-night box. In go pyjamas. In goes the bedtime book. In goes [Name]'s favourite drawing. And last of all, [Object].
spreads.setting: Bedroom. [Name] packs a cardboard box: pyjamas, book, a child's crayon drawing, [Object] last. No family photos
spreads.art: Bedroom. [Name] packs a cardboard box: pyjamas, book, a child's crayon drawing, [Object] last. No family photos
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: The big van comes. Strong people carry the beds and the sofa and all the boxes. The first-night box comes in the car, packed where they can find it first.
spreads.setting: Kerbside: removal van with people carrying the sofa
spreads.art: Kerbside: removal van with people carrying the sofa; the building is out of frame. [Name] in an age-appropriate car seat, harness on; the first-night box stowed separately in the boot, visible through the back window
spreads.calm_zone_note: Sky — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Here it is: the new front door. A different colour. A different number. [Carer] gives [Name] the key. Click. The door swings open.
spreads.setting: New front door, different colour, no readable number, framed close so it could be a house or a flat. [Name] turns the key
spreads.art: New front door, different colour, no readable number, framed close so it could be a house or a flat. [Name] turns the key; [Carer] behind
spreads.calm_zone_note: Above the door — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Inside, the rooms are empty. "Hello!" calls [Name]. "Hello… hello… hello…" say the empty rooms. [Name] laughs. The rooms laugh too. Well, they echo.
spreads.setting: Empty room. [Name] calls out, hands cupped, laughing
spreads.art: Empty room. [Name] calls out, hands cupped, laughing
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: This is [Name]'s new room. "It doesn't look like my old room," says [Name]. "Not yet," says [Carer]. "We can make it ours together. Where shall your bed go?" "By that wall. So I can still see the sky."
spreads.setting: New bedroom. [Name] stands thoughtful, then points to a wall away from the window
spreads.art: New bedroom. [Name] stands thoughtful, then points to a wall away from the window; [Carer] holds the bed frame. Window with no dangling cords near the bed
spreads.calm_zone_note: Window — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Before anything else, [Name] opens the first-night box. Pyjamas on the bed. Bedtime book on the pillow. Favourite drawing on the wall. [Object] in the middle of it all.
spreads.art: [Name] opens the box; pyjamas on the bed, book on the pillow, the drawing taped to the wall, [Object] in the middle
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Dinner is on the floor, with two big moving boxes for a table. Beans on toast, eaten straight from the plates on [Name]'s knees. "This is the best restaurant," says [Name].
spreads.setting: Floor dinner, two big moving boxes as a table (not the first-night box), beans on toast
spreads.art: Floor dinner, two big moving boxes as a table (not the first-night box), beans on toast
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: At bedtime, the ceiling is different. The walls are different. But the bedtime book is the same. The pyjamas are the same. And so is the goodnight kiss.
spreads.setting: Bedtime in the new room: new ceiling and walls, same pyjamas, [Carer] reading the same book. Bed against the wall, away from the window
spreads.art: Bedtime in the new room: new ceiling and walls, same pyjamas, [Carer] reading the same book. Bed against the wall, away from the window
spreads.calm_zone_note: Wall — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: In the morning, [Name] looks out of the new window. A girl across the road waves. [Name] waves back. And down the road, there's a park with a red slide.
spreads.setting: Morning, seen through the new window (a view that works from a house or a flat). A girl across the road waves
spreads.art: Morning, seen through the new window (a view that works from a house or a flat). A girl across the road waves; a park with a red slide further down. A generic street, never the family's real neighbourhood
spreads.calm_zone_note: Sky — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Name] draws the old home: the old door, the old window, the old step. [Carer] sticks it on the new wall. "I can keep both," says [Name].
spreads.setting: [Name]'s drawing of the old home taped to the new wall
spreads.art: [Name]'s drawing of the old home taped to the new wall; [Name] points at it
spreads.calm_zone_note: Wall — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: That afternoon, [Name] goes back to the new front door and knocks. Knock, knock. [Carer] opens it wide. "Welcome home," says [Carer]. And it is.
spreads.setting: A doorstep game, framed close (house or flat): [Name] one step outside the open door, knocking on it
spreads.art: A doorstep game, framed close (house or flat): [Name] one step outside the open door, knocking on it; [Carer] right there in the doorway, opening it wide. Never alone outside
spreads.calm_zone_note: Above the door — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

parent_spread.you_could_say: "Our things are coming with us, and so are we."
parent_spread.try_together: "What will you put in your first-night box?"
parent_spread.in_real_life: Pack a first-night box together with familiar things, and keep as much of your usual bedtime routine as you can.
parent_spread.read_it_again: Read this story a few nights in a row, and once more just before the day itself.
